questions.question: What factors are used to determine the proper type of aircraft fabric covering material for an aircraft?
questions.idealAnswer: The original material is used provided by the type certificate data sheet, however FAA exceptions exist a Supplemental Type Certificate (STC) may be used. A field approval from the local Flight Standard District Office (FSDO), this is only a one time approval. A form 337 must be filled out for a field approval.

questions.question: What are some of the approved aircraft fabric coverings and systems?
questions.idealAnswer: Ceconite, Polyfiber, Superflight, Air tech, Stewert system, Randolph system, Stits/ Polly Fiber. These manufactures are FAA- Parts Manufactured Authorized or FAA (PMA) This includes tapes, liquids, lacing chord, threads and various other products to produce a strong and durable outer covering for the aircraft being covered.

questions.question: What kind of seams are used in aircraft fabric coverings?
questions.idealAnswer: Envelope method and blanket method are used. Doped or glued seams may be used following (STC) Approval methods. Sewn seams include the French-fell or folded fell seam types.

questions.question: Explain the terms, warp, fill, and bias as they refer to aircraft fabric.
questions.idealAnswer: The warp of the fabric is the direction along the length of the fabric. the fill or weave is the direction across the width of the fabric. the fabric bias is diagonal to the the warp and fill. These terms can be used to refer to the fibers that make up the fabric.

questions.question: Why is structure surface preparation important and when is this performed?
questions.idealAnswer: Polyester fabric can last for years before recovering, so it is imperative when fabric is removed to accomplish a thorough inspection, cleaning and any repairs be completed. An Airframe Powerplant technician holding Inspection Authorization (IA) may be needed to approve any major repairs or alterations before recovering is performed.

questions.question: How is the fabric covering attached to the Airframe?
questions.idealAnswer: A polyester type fabric covering is attached with cement or glued to the airframe structure at all points where it makes contact. Special formula adhesives have replaced nitrate dope. The exception are the wings, they may be cemented but also secure with screws, rivets, clips, and lacing chord depending on the specifics of the approved method by the manufacturer.

questions.idealAnswer: Aircraft coverings are effected most by UV light, therefore the upper covering that is exposed to the sun must be protected with UV sealer coats and UV inhibitors sprayed on during the finishing process.

questions.idealAnswer: Make sure to inspect the damage closely to make sure there is no damage to the structure. questions.question: What is the preferred seam used when machine sewing pieces of aircraft fabric together?
questions.idealAnswer: The French fell seam.

questions.question: What are two types of fabric used to cover aircraft?
questions.idealAnswer: Polyester and cotton.

questions.question: What type of hand sewing stitch is used when sewing in a panel of new fabric on an aircraft fabric covered wing?
questions.idealAnswer: A baseball stitch, Locked every eight to ten stitches.

questions.question: What is the term for a piece of wood that has deteriorated to the point where when you crush it, it will turn to a dry powder?
questions.idealAnswer: Dry rot.

questions.question: What are three types of fabric that can be used to cover an aircraft?
questions.idealAnswer: Cotton, synthetic (Dacron), and glass fabrics.

questions.question: What paperwork must be completed if an aircraft that was originally covered with Grade-A cotton is re-covered using a synthetic fabric?
questions.idealAnswer: An STC and a Form 337 must be completed.

questions.question: What type of rib lacing cord is recommended for attaching cotton fabric to an aircraft structure?
questions.idealAnswer: Waxed linen cord is recommended.

questions.question: How wide should the surface tape be that is used to cover the trailing edge of an aircraft wing?
questions.idealAnswer: It should be three inches wide.

questions.question: Why is the surface tape used on trailing edge of the control surfaces of some airplanes notched?
questions.idealAnswer: If the tape starts to lift (due to edges facing into the wind), the tape will tear off at the notch instead of tearing off in a long strip, which could create excessive drag by spoiling.

questions.idealAnswer: To keep the rib lacing cord from pulling through the fabric.

questions.question: Should a sewed seam in the fabric used to cover an aircraft wing run spanwise or chordwise?
questions.idealAnswer: Chordwise is preferred , but both can be used.

questions.question: What is the preferred seam used for machine sewing pieces of aircraft fabric together?

questions.question: What type of knot is used for locking the stitches used for rib lacing on a fabric-covered wing?

questions.question: What type of hand-sewing stitch is used for a panel of new fabric on fabric-covered wings?
questions.idealAnswer: A Baseball stitch locked with a (half-hitch knot) every 8-10 stitches, 1/4 inch apart.

questions.question: What is the minimum strength aircraft fabric is allowed to deteriorate before considered unairworthy?
questions.idealAnswer: It can deteriorate down to 70% of the required strength for that aircraft . Example: Cotton 80psi typical can deteriorate down to 56psi or 80 x 0.70 = (56).

questions.question: What is an anti-tear strip, and when is it required on fabric-covered aircraft?
questions.idealAnswer: On aircraft with a VNE more than 250mph, they are used under the wing rib stitching and are a strip of the same type of fabric used for the wings. They are placed leading edge to trailing edge in the (prop wash/slip stream) plus one wing rib. Outside of the prop wash they are place at the forward spar to trailing edge on top of the wing, and not needed on the bottom of the wing.

questions.question: When are drainage grommets applied when an aircraft is being re-covered?
questions.idealAnswer: At the same time surface tape is applied; laid into the third coat of dope.

questions.question: Where are drainage grommets located on a fabric-covered wing?
questions.idealAnswer: At the lowest point in each bay; on each side of a wing rib on the wing underside at trailing edge.

questions.question: How is the strength of the fabric on an aircraft structure determined?
questions.idealAnswer: Using an FAA-approved fabric punch tester (Maule or Seybolt), or laboratory pull-testing of a 1” wide sample.

questions.idealAnswer: Keeps the fabric from sticking to structure when the first coat of dope is applied; fabric normally sags enough to touch the structure before it begins to pull taut.
